cards.title: I've got feelings for a teacher at my children's school
cards.body: A parent grapples with unexpected romantic feelings while married with two children. The column explores whether crushes that feel freeing outside everyday life should be acted upon.

cards.title: I'm giving birth as maternity care in Ireland transforms
cards.body: A mother shares her experience navigating Ireland's two-tier maternity system during labor. She highlights how unfair private systems are finally giving way to universal state care despite resistance from private interests.

cards.title: Music festivals aren't festivals without children
cards.body: A parent defends bringing toddlers to music festivals, arguing families add magic rather than spoil the fun. She shares how her perspective on spontaneity changed after having twins.

cards.title: Are you calling your college freshman too much?
cards.body: Parents face the challenge of staying connected with college-bound kids without becoming overbearing. These guidelines help navigate the delicate balance of independence and involvement.

cards.title: The 10 minutes after your child loses it matter most
cards.body: How parents respond immediately after a child's emotional breakdown is crucial to their recovery. Most parents accidentally make things worse during this critical calming-down window.

cards.title: Practical parenting tools for traumatized children
cards.body: Dr. Karyn Purvis and Lisa Qualls provide methods for addressing the exceptional needs of adopted and foster children. The approach emphasizes calm, firm, and respectful parenting strategies.

cards.title: How sports' soft skills nourish lifetime success
cards.body: Youth sports once consistently trained soft skills like teamwork and resilience, but this coaching has become nearly extinct. These competencies are essential for children's long-term development.

cards.title: Meta's settlement isn't as good for kids as it seems
cards.body: While the Meta settlement appears to be a win for children's mental health, it falls short in significant ways. The agreement doesn't target root causes and may not go far enough to protect young users.
